Someone Paid Just $8,900 for a Tesla Model S, No Typo Here
13 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Gone are the days when the Tesla Model S was associated with deep-pocketed people, as the battery-electric sedan can now cost new (electric) bicycle money.
The average value tends to sit between $10,000 and over $100,000 for such a thing. It all depends on the model year, powertrain, mileage, and overall condition, and near-new trims, especially the neck-snappingly fast Plaid, can easily venture into the six-digit territor.
But this one is not a Plaid, nor a new model year example, as you are looking at a 2014 Tesla Model S 70. It has a clean California title, has never been crashed, and the odometer read 79,200 miles (~127,500 km) at the time of cataloging.
The known flaws category of the ad reveals that there are scuffs, dings, chips, and scratches on the outside, as well as a peeling finish on the left front door panel window switches, and creases and stains on the upholstery. Therefore, this EV has definitely seen a lot of usage. The tires carry 2020 and 2021 date codes, the listing shows.
According to the listing, which quotes the selling dealer, the battery capacity has increased to 70 kWh, and this, alongside the tinted windows, is the only notable modification.
Photo: Cars&Bids Power is supplied by a single electric motor, which is estimated to have produced 315 horsepower and 325 pound-feet (440 Nm) of torque or so when the car was new. The EPA-estimated driving range of this model was 234 miles (377 km) when it was still being sold.
This older Tesla Model S features a Red Multi-Coat exterior color on top of the tan interior. It rides on 21-inch Turbine wheels, has a 17-inch touchscreen display, piano black trim on the inside, power-adjustable seats at the front, rear-facing third-row seats, and a power sunroof.
In addition to the car, the new owner will get one key, and that is it. The vendor is a dealer that reportedly bought the electric sedan in June 2026, adding some 300 miles (~500 km) since. The selling price is not a surprise anymore, given that we mentioned it in the title, and just in case you missed it, here it is: $8,900.
The Tesla Model S in question was advertised at the excitement of no reserve on Cars&Bids as part of an online auction that ended on November 19, 2026. And we don’t know about you, but this is definitely a lot of car for the money, though it is something that not many people would have dared to buy. Are you one of them? Would you have bought this EV if you saw it advertised for $8,900? Tell us all about it in the comments area below, and then check out this ride in more detail here .
